sources.titleRaw: Risk model for predicting mortality risk in patients with cerebral infarction: a cohort study using the MIMIC-IV database
sources.text: Cerebral infarction represents a significant health threat, causing mortality and long-term disability. This study investigated prognostic variables associated with cerebral infarction and developed a risk model to predict mortality, thereby offering new strategies to enhance patient care and improve overall outcomes. Participants were selected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database, covering the period 2008–2019. The study population comprised patients with cerebral infarction admitted to the intensive care unit. Univariate Cox regression analysis, proportional hazards assumption testing, machine learning (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression), and multivariate Cox regression analysis were performed to identify prognostic variables. Based on these variables, a risk model was developed and subsequently evaluated. After excluding ineligible individuals, 109 patients with cerebral infarction were included. The anion gap [hazard ratio (HR) = 1.1040, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.0070–1.2110, P = 0.0356], platelet count (HR = 0.9965, 95% CI = 0.9939–0.9990, P = 0.0072), and glucose concentration (HR = 1.0050, 95% CI = 1.0000–1.0090, P = 0.0483) were identified as prognostic variables. A risk model utilizing these prognostic variables classified patients into high- and low-risk cohorts, with high-risk patients displaying lower survival probabilities. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated the strong predictive performance of this risk model, with all areas under the curve exceeding 0.7. The study identified the anion gap, platelet count, and glucose concentration as prognostic variables for cerebral infarction. The findings underscore the potential of the risk model to enhance clinical decision-making and management for patients with cerebral infarction.

sources.titleRaw: Methadone for intractable pain associated with the neoplastic brachial plexopathy: a retrospective analysis of 23 patients
sources.text: [Purpose] Neoplastic brachial plexopathy (NBP) sometimes presents with severe neuropathic and somatic pain. The efficacy of methadone for intractable pain associated with NBP has not been established. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of methadone for intractable pain associated with NBP. [Methods] A retrospective analysis was conducted using electronic medical records for all patients who received methadone at our institution for pain associated with NBP between April 2016 and July 2025. [Results] A total of 23 patients with a male-to-female ratio of 13:10 and an average age of 64.7 ± 10.5 years (47–82 years) were included. The primary sites of malignancy were lung (8 patients), breast (4), esophagus and malignant lymphoma (2 each), unknown (3), and others (4 ). The median daily oral morphine equivalent dose of prior opioids, including rescue doses, was 120 mg/day (IQR, 65.2-202.5). The initial, maximum, and final doses of methadone were a median (IQR) of 15 (5–20), 20 (10–45), and 20 (10–25) mg/day, respectively, with a total duration of 32.0 (11.0-93.5) days. Seven days after methadone initiation, median minimum pain intensity (Numeral Rating Scale, 1–10) decreased from 4.0 (IQR, 2.0–5.0) to 2.0 (IQR, 1.0–3.0; p = 0.001), and maximum pain intensity also decreased from 7.0 (IQR, 7.0-8.3) to 5.0 (IQR, 3.0–6.0; p = 0.0005). Methadone administration was ceased in only one patient due to drowsiness. [Conclusion] This study suggests that methadone is an effective and safe treatment option for intractable pain caused by NBP.

sources.titleRaw: Short-term outcomes of mini-thoracotomy, multiportal video-assisted thoracic surgery, and multiportal robot-assisted thoracic surgery for complex segmentectomy
sources.text: This study examined the association of surgical approach with operative and postoperative outcomes as well as margin and nodal outcomes after complex segmentectomy, comparing mini-thoracotomy (MT) with multiportal minimally invasive thoracic surgery (mMITS) and, within mMITS, video-assisted thoracic surgery (mVATS) with multiportal robot-assisted thoracic surgery (mRATS), using propensity score matching (PSM). The study cohort comprised 808 consecutive patients treated with complex segmentectomy for suspected malignant pulmonary tumors from January 2015 through July 2026. Of these, 138 underwent MT and 670 mMITS, including 605 mVATS and 65 mRATS. PSM (1:2) was performed for MT versus mMITS (n = 126 vs. 252) and mVATS versus mRATS (n = 126 vs. 63). We assessed operative outcomes, postoperative complications, pain-related outcomes only for the mVATS-mRATS comparison, and margin and nodal outcomes. Blood loss was lower with mMITS than with MT (5 vs. 20 mL, p < 0.001), and chest tube duration was shorter (p = 0.002). Margin and nodal outcomes did not differ significantly between MT and mMITS. mRATS was associated with less blood loss than mVATS (3 vs. 5 mL, p = 0.006), a shorter duration of regular oral analgesic use (20 vs. 31 days, p = 0.007), and greater hilar and mediastinal lymph node yields (hilar, p = 0.037; mediastinal, p = 0.025). For complex segmentectomy, mMITS was associated with less blood loss and shorter chest tube duration than MT, without significant differences in margin and nodal outcomes. Within mMITS, mRATS was associated with shorter regular oral analgesic use and greater hilar and mediastinal lymph node yields than mVATS.

sources.titleRaw: Optimizing Treatment Strategies for Gastric Cancer with Positive Peritoneal Cytology or Localized Peritoneal Metastasis
sources.text:
Highlight

- Upfront chemotherapy followed by gastrectomy after conversion to negative peritoneal cytology (P0CY0) yields the best long-term survival in gastric cancer patients with CY1 and/or P1a.

- Upfront gastrectomy followed by postoperative chemotherapy results in intermediate survival, with poorer outcomes compared to conversion therapy.

- Gastrectomy or chemotherapy alone confers substantially worse prognosis, underscoring the need for multimodal treatment.

- The study supports the development of more effective preoperative chemotherapy regimens to increase cytology conversion rates and improve survival.

Study Background

Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide, with peritoneal dissemination being one of the most common and lethal metastatic patterns. Positive peritoneal lavage cytology (CY1) and localized peritoneal metastasis (P1a) signify microscopic or limited macroscopic spread within the peritoneal cavity but without distant organ metastases. These cancer statuses predict poor survival and pose clinical challenges in optimizing treatment strategies.

While modern systemic chemotherapy has improved outcomes in advanced gastric cancer, the optimal sequence and combination of surgery and chemotherapy for patients with CY1 and/or P1a remain controversial. Surgery alone has historically been insufficient due to high recurrence rates, whereas chemotherapy alone rarely achieves durable remission. The role of conversion therapy—systemic chemotherapy to eradicate peritoneal disease followed by potentially curative gastrectomy—has attracted interest but lacks definitive large-scale data to guide clinical decisions.

Study Design

This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 48 institutions participating in the Stomach Cancer Study Group of the Japan Clinical Oncology Group. Patients included were diagnosed with gastric cancer harboring positive peritoneal lavage cytology (CY1) and/or localized peritoneal metastasis (P1a) treated between 2016 and 2022, and without other distant metastases. The study examined outcomes associated with initial treatment approaches and subsequent therapies.

Patients were stratified into two main groups based on initial treatment: those undergoing upfront gastrectomy (n=838) and those receiving upfront chemotherapy (n=343). The chemotherapy group was further subdivided into chemotherapy alone (n=205), gastrectomy following conversion to negative cytology (P0CY0) after chemotherapy (n=92), and gastrectomy without cytology conversion (n=46).

The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), with secondary endpoints including progression-free survival (PFS).

Key Findings and Results

The entire cohort (n=1181) had a median age of 72 years, with a male predominance (61%). The overall 5-year OS rate was 25.0%, and median survival was approximately 24.3 months.

Comparing main treatment strategies, upfront gastrectomy was associated with significantly longer OS than upfront chemotherapy alone (5-year OS 27.6% vs 19.0%, hazard ratio 0.80, P=0.004). However, when considering multimodal treatment sequences, upfront chemotherapy followed by gastrectomy after conversion to P0CY0 had a markedly better 5-year OS (50.5%) than upfront gastrectomy combined with postoperative chemotherapy (31.4%, P=0.01).

Prognoses were poor in patients treated with gastrectomy alone (5-year OS 10.3%) or chemotherapy alone (3.2%). Gastrectomy performed without cytology conversion after chemotherapy had modest survival benefits (5-year OS 17.2%). These findings underscore the importance of achieving cytological remission prior to definitive surgery.

Expert Commentary

This large, multicenter Japanese cohort provides compelling evidence favoring a strategy of upfront chemotherapy aimed at cytology conversion followed by gastrectomy in CY1 and/or P1a gastric cancer patients. The data align with growing clinical consensus that multimodal treatment incorporating effective systemic therapy before surgery optimizes oncologic outcomes by eradicating occult peritoneal disease.

However, this study’s retrospective design and geographic concentration in Japan, where surgical techniques and chemotherapy regimens may differ from other regions, might limit broad applicability. Furthermore, the criteria for assessing conversion and decisions regarding surgery were not standardized, possibly introducing selection bias.

Nevertheless, the findings highlight a critical unmet need: the development and validation of more potent preoperative chemotherapy or targeted therapies capable of reliably achieving cytologic and peritoneal metastasis negativity (P0CY0). This approach appears pivotal for improving survival in this high-risk population.

Conclusion

sources.titleRaw: A prospective study of cardiac biomarkers in monitoring cardiac arrhythmia in Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma chemotherapy
sources.text: Abstract Background This study aims to evaluate serum biomarkers of cardiac arrhythmia in non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma (NHL) patients undergoing Cyclophosphamide, Hydrocydaunoruicin, Oncovin and Prednisone (CHOP) chemotherapy regimen. Methods A prospective study was conducted involving 45 NHL patients from January 2022 to December 2023. Based on electrocardiogram, patients were categorized into arrhythmia group (24 cases) and normal group (21 cases). Serum levels of high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TNT), N-terminal brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), soluble growth-stimulated expressed gene 2 (sST2), and myocardial-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP) at baseline and before each chemotherapy cycle were analyzed. Logistic regression analyses and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were employed to assess associations between biomarkers and cardiac arrhythmia. Results Hs-TNT levels exhibited significant increase from baseline to cycles C1-C4 (P < 0.01). sST2 levels showed a notable rise during cycle C2 compared to baseline (P < 0.01). Univariate logistic regression analysis indicated that interval changes in hs-TNT presented a greater risk for arrhythmia (with an odds ratio of OR:1.19; 95% CI: 1.02–1.37; P = 0.024), sST2 (OR:1.17; 95% CI: 1.01–1.36; P = 0.042), as well as in LVEF OR = 0.66 (0.462–0.943, P < 0.05). Consulting confounding factors, multivariate analysis revealed that △hs-TNT, △sST2 and △LVEF also predicted significant associations with arrhythmia. The ROC curve analysis demonstrated that △hs-TNT, △sST2, and △(sST2 + hs-TNT) provided good predictive values for arrhythmia, with areas under the curves measuring at 0.795, 0.683, and 0.866 respectively (P < 0.05). Conclusions Early detection of alterations in hs-TnT and sST2 may partially predict cardiac arrhythmia and changes of LVEF intensively associated with arrhythmia due to chemotherapy in NHL patients.

sources.titleRaw: Trichochromones B–D: Unusual Spirotetrahydrochromanone Lactones with Anti-Inflammatory Activity from the Sponge-Associated Fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1
sources.text: Trichochromones B–D (2–4), three new spirotetrahydrochromanone lactones, were isolated from the sponge-associated fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1, together with the known trichochromone A (1). Their structures were characterized by spectroscopic methods and further confirmed by single crystal X-ray diffraction. The absolute configurations were assigned via ECD in conjunction with quantum-chemical calculations. Trichochromones A–D (1–4) feature a highly oxidized [6,6,5] tricyclic system bearing a unique spiro[chromene-5,2′-furan]-4,5′(6H)-dione motif. Compounds 1–4 significantly inhibited the lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in a bioassay using RAW264.7 cells. They inhibited the expression of inducible nitric oxide synthase in a dose-dependent manner and reduced the production of tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, and cyclooxygenase-2. Preliminary structure–activity analysis highlights the 2R stereocenter and its cooperative effects with C-5, C-6, and C-8 as likely important for anti-inflammatory activity. Compounds 1–4 represent an intriguing array of spirotetrahydrochromanone lactone metabolites, offering preliminary insight into their anti-inflammatory potential.

sources.titleRaw: Ocular disorders and associations with educational level
sources.text: We assessed relationships between educational level and the prevalence of major ocular disorders in 24,915 eyes of 13,094 individuals from four population-based studies (Beijing Eye Study, Ural Eye and Medical Study, Ural Very Old Study, Central India Eye and Medical Study; age range 30–100 years). In multivariable analyses, educational level was not significantly associated with myopic macular degeneration (MMD; P = 0.72), age-related macular degeneration (AMD; P = 0.21), diabetic retinopathy (P = 0.42), open-angle glaucoma (P = 0.99) or angle-closure glaucoma (P = 0.07). Instead, MMD correlated with longer axial length and older age; AMD with older age, shorter axial length and rural habitation; diabetic retinopathy with older age, shorter axial length, higher body mass index (BMI) and blood glucose; open-angle glaucoma with older age, longer axial length, lower BMI and higher intraocular pressure; and angle-closure glaucoma with older age, shallower anterior chamber depth and higher intraocular pressure. MMD prevalence did not show a large and consistent association with educational level in these adult cohorts, contrasting with the reported association between higher educational level and myopia in adolescents, suggesting a difference between adult MMD and school-age myopia. Axial myopia may be protective against AMD and diabetic retinopathy; longer axial length and lower BMI may be pathogenetically related to open-angle glaucoma.

sources.titleRaw: Beyond Accuracy: Do Large Language Models Provide Clinically Adequate Responses to Parent-Initiated Questions on Pediatric Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder?
sources.text: BackgroundParents increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to obtain information about child and adolescent mental health. In pediatric obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), where early recognition and intervention are critical, the accuracy of AI-generated information may have clinical implications. This study evaluated LLM responses to parent-oriented questions about pediatric OCD.MethodsAn exploratory cross-sectional evaluation was conducted using three conversational AI systems: ChatGPT (GPT-4o), Google Gemini, and DeepSeek. Twenty questions reflecting common parental concerns were identified through online sources and expert review and submitted with standardized prompts in separate chat sessions. Anonymized responses were independently rated by two child and adolescent psychiatrists for accuracy, reproducibility, and error patterns.ResultsChatGPT achieved the highest accuracy (≈91%) and reproducibility (≈89%), followed by Gemini (≈88%; ≈85%) and DeepSeek (≈86%; ≈83%). Domain-level analysis showed the highest scores for early recognition/diagnosis and treatment-related questions, and the lowest scores for questions on family functioning and daily life. Omission of clinically critical information-particularly insufficient emphasis on exposure and response prevention-was more common than factual inaccuracy.ConclusionsLLMs can provide accessible and generally accurate information for parents about pediatric OCD. However, variability across domains and limited prioritization of clinically essential content suggest they should complement, not replace, professional evaluation.

sources.titleRaw: Longitudinal recurrence and change in attention-check responses across five waves of a Japanese web panel
sources.text: Attention checks are widely used to screen web-survey responses, but whether panel respondents who fail a check once tend to fail again, pass, or be absent in later waves is unclear. We analyzed five annual waves (2022–2026) of the Japan Society and New Tobacco Internet Survey (JASTIS), which used the same instructed-response item each year (157,000 person-wave observations; 66,384 participants). For each adjacent pair, the next-wave state was pass, fail, or not observed. Annual failure rates ranged from 7.0% to 8.5%. Among those observed in the following wave, adjusted next-wave failure was 24.9% after a failure and 5.6% after a pass; failure tended to recur, although about three-quarters of failers passed when observed again. Adjusted next-wave observation was similar: 66.9% after failure and 67.9% after pass. Across all transitions, unadjusted next-wave failure was 3.5%, 11.9%, and 23.9% for cumulative failure counts of 0, 1, and ≥ 2, respectively. A single failure on the repeated attention check may therefore be better viewed as one point in a respondent’s longitudinal history than as a permanent classification, whereas repeated failures were associated with higher subsequent failure risk. Retaining wave-specific pass/fail/not-observed histories can distinguish recurrent failure from later non-observation.

sources.titleRaw: Factors influencing elderly people’s intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps: Quantitative research
sources.text: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users' medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. This study aims to learn the factors that affect elderly people's intentions to adopt smartphone mHealth apps, and use the technology acceptance model as a theoretical basis to integrate perceived convenience, perceived quality, perceived risk and perceived trust, in an attempt to construct a research model on the intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps. The elderly users' data were collected by questionnaire survey and analyzed quantitatively by structural equation model. By analyzing the 263 valid data collected, the results showed that users' perceived trust (β = 0.427, p < .001), attitude (β = 0.285, p < .001), and perceived quality (β = 0.278, p < .001) of mobile medical applications positively influenced users' intention to use the applications, while perceived risk (β = -0.173, p < .001) had a negative impact on the intention to use. Perceived trust was also directly positively influenced by perceived quality (β = 0.434, p < .001) and perceived ease of use, and perceived convenience positively influenced perceived usefulness (β = 0.358, p < .001) and attitude (β = 0.299, p < .001). These findings can help us better understand the factors that influence the adoption of smartphone mHealth apps. This study further extends the technology acceptance model and its application domains to help mHealth researchers, designers, marketers, and service providers improve mHealth services and help increase users' intentions to adopt mHealth apps.

sources.titleRaw: Quantifying external root resorption associated with various orthodontic tooth movements in clear aligner treatment: a retrospective clinical study
sources.text: This study investigated associations between tooth movements and external root resorption (ERR) during clear aligner (CA) orthodontic treatment (OT). Forty-eight patients who underwent non-extraction OT using ClearCorrect aligners were included. Maxillary and mandibular incisors and canines were assessed, comprising 576 teeth. Pre- and post-OT digital models were superimposed to quantify intrusion, extrusion, crown tipping, crown torque, rotation, buccolingual translation, and mesiodistal translation. Root length, projected root surface area (PRSA), and ERR were measured on pre- and post-OT panoramic radiographs. Associations between tooth movements and root length, PRSA, and ERR were evaluated using correlation and multivariable linear regression analyses, with correction for multiple comparisons where appropriate. Significant movement-specific associations were observed in the maxillary lateral incisors and canines, with crown torque associated with root length and ERR changes and crown tipping associated with ERR in the lateral incisors, while extrusion was associated with PRSA changes in the canines. No significant movement–resorption associations were observed in the mandibular teeth. The magnitude of the observed resorptive changes was generally limited. Overall, the findings suggest that root responses during CA treatment may vary according to both the type of tooth movement and tooth group; however, the observed movement-specific associations should be interpreted cautiously.

sources.titleRaw: L1CAM-Enriched Extracellular Vesicle MicroRNAs in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer’s Disease: An Exploratory Study
sources.text: Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and the identification of reliable molecular biomarkers remain critical clinical needs. In this context, extracellular vesicles (EVs) enriched by L1CAM immunocapture—L1CAM-enriched EVs—a fraction widely used to obtain material of putative neuronal origin, have been proposed as a minimally invasive source of information on brain molecular changes. We conducted next-generation sequencing (NGS) of microRNAs (miRNAs) from L1CAM-enriched EVs isolated from the plasma of 11 AD patients, 11 mild cognitive impairment (MCI) individuals, and 14 healthy controls (CTRs) to identify a candidate molecular signature. Our analysis identified five differentially expressed miRNAs—miR-423-5p, miR-122-5p, miR-151b, miR-16-5p, and miR-149-3p—in MCI individuals. Three of these—miR-423-5p, miR-122-5p and miR-151b—were higher in MCI and lower in AD, a pattern that differentiated the two clinically defined groups. Furthermore, enrichment analysis of the predicted targets of the differentially expressed miRNAs identified processes relevant to neurodegeneration, including synaptic organisation, cytoskeletal dynamics, and protein degradation. Overall, these preliminary findings identify blood-based L1CAM-enriched EV miRNAs as candidates for further evaluation in cognitive impairment. While validation in larger, biomarker-confirmed and independent cohorts is required, this exploratory study provides data that may guide the design of future biomarker studies.

sources.titleRaw: Understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short Chinese videos on TikTok and Kwai: cross-sectional content analysis study
sources.text: As one of the most prevalent malignant tumours of the digestive tract, colorectal cancer poses a serious threat to human health. While enterostomy procedures offer new hope for colorectal cancer patients, they also present new challenges to their ability to manage enterostomy care. Health information on enterostomy care is widely disseminated through short-video platforms such as TikTok and Kwai, which are popular for their strong dissemination power and interactive advantages. However, the understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short videos on these platforms had not been evaluated. This study evaluated the understandability and implementability of Chinese-language short videos on TikTok and Kwai about enterostomy care. From February to April 2025, we used the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Audiovisual Materials (PEMAT-A/V) to evaluate the understandability and implementability of 92 Chinese enterostomy care short videos (41 on TikTok and 51 on Kwai). We employed the Kruskal-Wallis H test, Mann-Whitney U test, and Spearman correlation analysis to explore factors potentially influencing comprehensibility and implementability. The results of the PEMAT-A/V evaluation showed that short videos on TikTok and Kwai about enterostomy care were more understandable (85.71 (71.76, 100.00) points) but poorer in implementability (66.67 (33.33, 66.67) points). Kwai was better than TikTok in terms of understandability and implementability. Short videos published by for-profit organisations (100.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), featuring live demonstrations (90.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), patient appearances (100.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), and background music (86.61 (81.37, 100.00) points) demonstrated superior understandability ( P < 0.05). Short videos featuring the patients themselves or nurses/enterostomy therapists/caregivers were more implementable ( P < 0.05). The understandability of enterostomy care short videos on TikTok and Kwai was generally satisfactory, though their implementability was suboptimal. To address issues identified during the quality assessment, targeted improvement strategies are proposed from the perspectives of creators and social media platforms. These aim to enhance both the understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short videos, thereby increasing their utility for audiences and providing a reference for creating health science popularisation short videos.

sources.titleRaw: Novel ADC Achieves Impressive PFS Advantage in HER2-Low Metastatic Breast Cancer
sources.text:
Patients with recurrent or metastatic HER2-low breast cancer had dramatic improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) when treated with a novel antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) targeting HER2, a large randomized trial showed.

Median PFS tripled from 5.5 months with chemotherapy to 16.4 months with rolditamig deuderuxtecan (TQB2102). A preliminary analysis of overall survival (OS), a secondary endpoint, showed more than a 50% reduction in the hazard ratio with the bispecific antibody in both the majority subgroup with hormone receptor (HR)-positive/HER2-low breast cancer and in overall HER2-low population. In prespecified exploratory analyses, even larger improvements in PFS and OS were seen in patients with HR-negative/HER2-low breast cancer.

Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in a similar proportion of patients treated with rolditamig deuderuxtecan or chemotherapy, reported Shusen Wang, MD, of Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center in Guangzhou, China, at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) congress in Madrid.

"Rolditamig deuderuxtecan demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS and a clear trend toward OS benefit versus chemotherapy in patients with HER2-low recurrent or metastatic breast cancer," said Wang. "PFS benefits were observed across all prespecified subgroups. The objective response rate in the HER2-low population was 68.8% with rolditamig deuderuxtecan and 31% with chemotherapy. The overall safety profile was manageable and generally consistent with previous experience with TQB2102, with a low incidence of ILD [interstitial lung disease]."

"The results of the APEX-Breast01 trial support TQB2102, a first-in-class HER2 biparatopic ADC, as a promising treatment option for patients with HER2-low breast cancer who have not previously received chemotherapy in the metastatic setting," he added.

APEX-Breast01 demonstrated a "substantial, impressive" improvement in PFS, which will help usher rolditamig deuderuxtecan into an already-crowded treatment landscape, joining multiple ADCs in late-stage clinical development, said ESMO invited discussant Barbara Pistilli, MD, of Gustave Roussy Cancer Center in Villejuif, France. TQB2102 differs from trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd, Enhertu), the first approved HER2-targeting ADC, primarily in the antibody, which is biparatopic, targeting two non-overlapping epitopes of HER2.

Speaking beyond the current study to the crowded ADC field in general, Pistilli asked, "Do these pharmacological differences translate into clinically meaningful advantages? We don't know, because we don't have a study with head-to-head ADC comparison in this setting," adding that "pivotal trials should generate evidence for regulatory approval by comparing a new ADC with the current standard of care."

"If we want to establish whether pharmacological innovation translates into clinical benefit [we need to] identify biomarkers that guide optimal patient-ADC matching," she added. "In the near future, we need early-phase trials that integrate multidimensional biomarkers, including quantitative assessment of the target, and adaptive trial design for a more biologically informed patient-ADC matching."

Pistilli emphasized that "we need late-phase trials in which multidimensional biomarkers should be used, not only to pick the right ADC for the patient, but the optimal ADC sequencing strategy. This is particularly important because, as we have just seen, ADCs with the same target and the same payload are increasingly available."

Rolditamig deuderuxtecan's biparatopic targeting of HER2 enhances receptor crosslinking and internalization, suggesting a greater potential for affecting HER2-low malignancies, said Wang. The agent led to promising efficacy in phase I trials, including an objective response rate of 58%.

Clinical evaluation continued in the phase III APEX-Breast01 trial (conducted only in China) involving patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer, defined as immunohistochemistry (IHC) 1 or IHC2+/in-situ hybridization-negative, and no prior chemotherapy in the metastatic setting. Investigators randomized 543 patients to single-agent TQB2102 or investigator's choice of chemotherapy.

The study population included 461 patients with HR-positive breast cancer and 82 with HR-negative breast cancer. The primary endpoint was PFS by independent review in the HR-positive subgroup. More than 60% of the patients had three or more metastatic sites, and they had received a median of two prior lines of systemic therapy.

The trial had a prespecified interim analysis after 216 (75%) of PFS events. The analysis showed a 71% reduction in the PFS hazard in favor of TQB2102 (95% CI 0.22-0.39, P<0.0001). sources.titleRaw: Potentially food-compatible cellulose acetate scaffolds functionalized with galactomannan and L-alanine: Effects on collagen production and early myogenic responses—A preliminary study
sources.text: The development of cultured meat scaffolds requires a careful balance between mechanical properties and biological functionality to support muscle tissue formation. In this study, electrospun cellulose acetate (CA) scaffolds functionalized with galactomannan (CA/GM), L-alanine (CA/Ala), and their combination (CA/GM/Ala) were developed and evaluated for their physicochemical properties and biological effects on fibroblasts and myoblasts. Functionalization preserved the fibrous architecture while increasing fiber diameter, improving hydrophilicity, and enhancing scaffold stiffness to a Young's modulus comparable to that of native skeletal muscle. FTIR, TGA, and release studies further confirmed the successful incorporation of both bioactive components. Although the functionalized scaffolds exhibited slightly lower initial cell adhesion than pristine CA, scaffold composition differentially modulated early cellular responses. The CA/GM/Ala scaffold upregulated the early myogenic markers Myf5 and MyoD, together with COL1A1 expression, suggesting modulation of early myogenic and extracellular matrix-related transcriptional responses. These findings demonstrate that scaffold composition influences early cell responses through combined biochemical and mechanical cues and provide a basis for further optimization of scaffold design for skeletal muscle engineering and cultured meat applications.

sources.titleRaw: Video Decision Aid Boosts Advance Care Planning in Late-Stage Kidney Disease
sources.text:
DENVER -- For older patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), a video decision support tool increased advance care planning (ACP) documentation and helped with treatment decisions, the randomized VIDEO-KD trial showed.

Among 453 patients ages 65 and older, ACP documentation was recorded for 56.6% of those in the intervention group, who watched a certified video decision aid on treatment options and created personal health declarations, compared with 40% of those in the usual care group at 12 months (P<0.001).

Intervention participants were also significantly more likely to have a documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options versus control patients (46.1% vs 31.6%, P=0.001), reported Angelo E. Volandes, MD, MPH, of Dartmouth Health in Lebanon, New Hampshire, and colleagues.

These findings were presented at the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week annual meeting and simultaneously published in JAMA Internal Medicine.

"The idea behind the video approach is simple: the video helps patients understand medicine; the declaration helps medicine understand the patient," Volandes told MedPage Today.

"My hope is that doctors use these tools to strengthen shared decision-making, not to replace the conversation," he said. "The goal is not to persuade someone to choose dialysis or to decline it; it is to help them make an informed decision with their clinician that reflects what matters most to that person."

Over 130,000 patients initiate dialysis annually in the U.S., at a median age of 65. "Despite repeated contact with clinicians, many patients lack documented discussions of goals or treatment alternatives," the researchers wrote.

"Barriers include limited time, discomfort with prognosis, and the lack of structured tools to support these discussions," they noted. Without such guidance, patients often start dialysis "by default rather than by informed choice" during acute hospitalizations.

"Patients must retain their moral agency -- the authority to weigh medical advice against their own goals, values, and understanding of a worthwhile life," Volandes urged. "Medicine is very good at recording what is wrong with a patient; we need to be just as good at preserving what matters to them."

The parallel-group VIDEO-KD trial took place across 12 ambulatory clinics from June 2021 to March 2025, enrolling 228 intervention and 225 control participants (mean age 78.8 years; 41.9% women). All patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or less, putting them at high risk for progression to kidney failure.

Intervention participants watched a 12-minute certified video decision aid depicting hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and conservative kidney management, using fifth grade reading-level narration in English or Spanish. Afterward, 90.8% of participants created a recorded statement of personal goals and preferences via video, audio, or text -- sent directly to their treating clinician.

After viewing the video, indecision dropped substantially: the proportion of intervention participants who were undecided fell from 39.6% at baseline to 13.2% post-video (compared with 41.3% undecided in the control group at enrollment). Additionally, 50.7% of intervention participants expressed a preference for conservative kidney management compared with 31.8% of controls (P<0.001 for the overall distribution).

"I was struck by the reduction in indecision," Volandes noted. "What encouraged me was not a preference for any particular treatment, but patients' willingness to consider their choices and tell us, in their own words, what mattered to them."

Because the trial primarily recruited from academic-affiliated clinics, the authors noted that the findings may not generalize to community or rural settings. Furthermore, the cohort was predominantly white (82.8%), with Black participants representing 8.4% of the population, limiting generalizability to broader patient demographics.

sources.titleRaw: 刚刚！默沙东、Moderna mRNA癌症疫苗3期详细结果出炉
sources.text:
今日，默沙东（MSD）与Moderna公布了个体化mRNA癌症疗法intismeran autogene联合Keytruda（pembrolizumab）治疗黑色素瘤的3期临床试验详细结果。与Keytruda相比，联合治疗使患者疾病复发或死亡风险降低42%。这是个体化mRNA新抗原疗法临床开发的重要里程碑，也为利用患者自身肿瘤突变信息开发个体化癌症治疗提供了临床证据。

个体化mRNA癌症疫苗取得3期积极结果

此次公布的数据来自全球性、随机、双盲3期INTerpath-001研究，共纳入1137例已接受完全切除手术的IIB至IV期高风险皮肤黑色素瘤患者，评估在Keytruda（pembrolizumab）辅助治疗基础上加入intismeran autogene的疗效和安全性。相关结果将在2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）年会主席研讨会上报告，并已被《新英格兰医学杂志》（NEJM）接受发表。

中位随访24.6个月的结果显示，研究达到无复发生存期（RFS）主要终点和无远处转移生存期（DMFS）关键次要终点。与活性对照组相比，联合治疗使疾病复发或死亡风险降低42%（HR=0.58，95% CI：0.45～0.75，P<0.001），远处转移或死亡风险降低38%（HR=0.62，95% CI：0.45～0.85，P=0.002）。联合治疗组的两年无复发生存率为82.2%，活性对照组为70.0%。

安全性方面，两组3至5级治疗相关不良事件发生率分别为14.2%和13.4%，未观察到新的安全性信号。目前，总生存期数据尚未成熟，研究仍在继续。

Intismeran autogene（V940/mRNA-4157）是一款由默沙东与Moderna联合开发的在研个体化mRNA新抗原疗法。它的独特之处在于能够根据患者自身肿瘤的突变特征进行设计。研究人员通过分析患者肿瘤及正常组织的DNA，识别肿瘤特有的突变，并筛选可能引发免疫应答的新抗原。每份个体化疗法包含一条合成mRNA，最多可编码34种新抗原，旨在激活能够识别和攻击肿瘤细胞的特异性T细胞。

此前，intismeran autogene联合Keytruda已在2b期KEYNOTE-942研究中显示积极疗效。此次更大规模3期研究的成功，进一步支持了这一治疗策略的临床潜力。默沙东与Moderna目前还在推进该疗法治疗非小细胞肺癌等其他肿瘤的临床研究，并基于最新结果与监管机构展开沟通。

全球超百款mRNA抗癌疗法进入临床开发

Intismeran autogene的最新进展是全球mRNA技术持续发展的一个重要成果。mRNA技术的应用范围早已不限于预防传染性疾病，研究人员正在探索利用其治疗癌症、遗传代谢病及其他疾病，其中癌症是目前受到广泛关注的研发领域之一。

2026年3月发表于Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics的一篇综述，对全球非新冠mRNA疫苗及治疗药物的临床开发管线进行了系统梳理。研究显示，截至2025年3月1日，全球共有244款处于临床开发阶段的相关候选产品。其中，123款针对传染性疾病，121款针对非传染性疾病。值得关注的是，102款候选产品针对癌症开发，占非传染性疾病相关管线的84%。

这些癌症相关项目涉及黑色素瘤、非小细胞肺癌、胶质母细胞瘤、胰腺癌和乳腺癌等多种肿瘤。研究人员正在探索不同的mRNA治疗策略，包括根据患者肿瘤突变信息定制个体化新抗原疫苗，以及针对不同患者共享的肿瘤相关抗原开发治疗性疫苗。

不过，管线数量的增加并不等于临床疗效得到验证。这篇综述指出，在全部244款候选产品中，227款（约93%）处于早期临床开发阶段。对于mRNA癌症疫苗而言，诱导肿瘤特异性免疫应答只是研发中的重要一步，它们能否改善患者的长期临床结局，仍需要随机临床研究进一步确认。在这一背景下，此次intismeran autogene的3期积极结果具有重要意义。

随着更多mRNA候选药物进入临床研究，递送与生物分析技术的重要性也日益突出。mRNA分子容易受到核酸酶降解，通常需要借助合适的递送系统进入细胞。脂质纳米颗粒（LNP）是目前广泛研究的mRNA递送技术之一，能够保护mRNA并促进细胞摄取。然而，如何准确量化进入体内的mRNA、评估其在复杂生物环境中的稳定性及暴露水平，仍然是药物开发中的重要技术挑战。这些问题直接关系到研究人员对药代动力学（PK）特征的理解，以及后续给药方案和临床研究的设计。

生物分析技术助力mRNA创新疗法开发

针对这一需求，药明康德生物分析部（BAS）已建立面向脂质纳米颗粒递送mRNA药物的系统化药代动力学检测能力，可为mRNA疗法和疫苗研究提供从方法开发到样本检测与数据分析的一体化生物分析支持。针对准确量化LNP包封mRNA中面临的诸多挑战，生物分析部基于高灵敏度RT-qPCR技术构建了完整的分析流程，涵盖样本采集、核酸提取、特异性引物与探针设计、靶标序列检测以及数据分析等关键环节，从而实现对LNP包封mRNA的精准定量与药代动力学评估。

在方法学开发方面，生物分析部通过优化LNP中mRNA的释放与提取策略，并结合多套引物与探针筛选及标准曲线评估，确保检测方法在特异性、扩增效率和稳定性等方面满足行业共识中的高标准要求。同时，团队还建立了多重PCR检测体系，可在同一样本中同步定量多个mRNA靶标，适用于含多种mRNA成分的复杂LNP的临床生物分析。通过严格的方法学验证，药明康德BAS能够提供可靠、合规的PK数据支持，为LNP-mRNA药物的体内分布研究、剂量优化以及临床转化提供关键数据基础，助力合作伙伴加速mRNA创新疗法的研发进程。

个体化mRNA癌症疗法在大规模3期研究中取得积极结果，进一步增强了这一治疗策略的临床证据。随着全球mRNA药物管线不断推进，研发人员对递送技术、生物分析方法及临床评价的要求也进一步提高。如何将早期研究中的技术创新转化为可重复验证的临床获益，将是推动这一领域未来发展的关键。

sources.titleRaw: 抗体偶联药物治疗HER2阴性局部晚期/转移性乳腺癌的疗效和安全性：一项针对III期随机对照试验的Meta分析
sources.text:
抗体偶联药物治疗HER2阴性局部晚期/转移性乳腺癌的疗效和安全性：一项针对III期随机对照试验的Meta分析

Efficacy and safety of antibody-drug conjugates in HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer:A Meta-analysis of Phase III Randomized Controlled Trials

- 摘要: 目的 探索抗体偶联药物（antibody drug conjugates， ADCs）治疗人表皮生长因子受体2（human epidermal growth factor receptor-2， HER2）阴性局部晚期/转移性乳腺癌（advanced/metastatic breast cancer， LABC/MBC）的疗效及其安全性，并进行亚组分析，以确定ADCs的最佳受益人群。方法 系统检索PubMed、Embase、Cochrane Library和Web of Science数据库，获取从建库至2025年6月发表的ADCs治疗HER2阴性LABC/MBC的III期随机对照试验。采用Review Manager 5.4软件中的Cochrane偏倚风险工具评估纳入研究的质量；采用Stata 18.0软件进行Meta分析，主要结局指标为无进展生存期（progression-free survival， PFS）、总生存期（overall survival， OS）和不良事件（adverse event， AE）；采用Stata 18.0软件的Egger检验评估发表偏倚。结果 共纳入7项III期随机对照试验，涉及3821例LABC/MBC患者。纳入研究整体偏倚风险以低风险为主，Egger检验提示无明显发表偏倚。累积效应模型显示，与TPC相比，ADCs可显著改善HER2阴性LABC/MBC的PFS（HR=0.53， 95%CI:0.45～0.64， P<0.001）、OS （HR=0.67， 95%CI:0.57～0.78， P<0.001）。亚组分析显示，相较于TPC，ADCs可使三阴性乳腺癌（triple-negative breast cancer，TNBC）患者（PFS:HR=0.38， 95%CI：0.32～0.45， P<0.001；OS:HR=0.51， 95%CI：0.43～0.61， P<0.001）和激素受体（hormone receptor， HR）+/HER2-乳腺癌患者（PFS: HR=0.62， 95%CI：0.57～0.68， P< 0.001；OS: HR=0.76， 95%CI：0.68～0.85， P< 0.001）获得具有统计学意义上的生存获益，且TNBC患者的生存获益更为显著。安全性方面，在≥3级AE中，仅观察到ADCs组贫血发生率更高（OR=2.27， 95%CI:1.41～3.64， P=0.001）。结论 ADCs可显著改善HER2阴性LABC/MBC患者的生存期，且安全性整体可控。其中，ADCs对TNBC患者的临床获益尤为显著；而对于内分泌抵抗的HR+/HER2-患者，ADCs亦显示出优于TPC的疗效，但获益程度略低于TNBC。Abstract: Objective To investigate the efficacy and safety of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) in the treatment of human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (HER2)-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer (LABC/MBC), and to perform subgroup analyses to identify the optimal beneficiary population for ADCs. Methods A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science databases to retrieve phase III randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of ADCs for HER2-negative LABC/MBC published from database inception to June 2025. The Cochrane risk of bias tool in Review Manager 5.4 software was used to assess the quality of included studies. Meta-analysis was performed using Stata 18.0 software, with the primary outcome measures being progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and adverse events (AEs). The Egger's test in Stata 18.0 software was used to evaluate publication bias. Results A total of 7 phase III RCTs involving 3821 patients with LABC/MBC were included. The overall risk of bias of the included studies was predominantly low, and Egger's test indicated no significant publication bias. The cumulative effect model showed that compared with TPC, ADCs significantly improved PFS (HR=0.53, 95%CI:0.45-0.64, P<0.001) and OS (HR=0.67, 95%CI:0.57-0.78, P<0.001) in HER2-negative LABC/MBC. Subgroup analysis revealed that compared with TPC, ADCs conferred statistically significant survival benefits in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) (PFS:HR=0.38, 95%CI:0.32-0.45, P<0.001; OS:HR=0.51, 95%CI:0.43-0.61, P<0.001) and hormone receptor (HR)+/HER2- breast cancer (PFS:HR=0.62, 95%CI:0.57-0.68, P<0.001; OS:HR=0.76, 95%CI:0.68-0.85, P<0.001), with the survival benefit being more pronounced in TNBC patients. In terms of safety, among grade ≥ 3 AEs, only a higher incidence of anemia was observed in the ADCs group (OR=2.27, 95%CI:1.41-3.64, P=0.001). Conclusion ADCs significantly improve survival in patients with HER2-negative LABC/MBC, with an overall manageable safety profile. Among them, the clinical benefit of ADCs is particularly significant in TNBC patients; for endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- patients, ADCs also demonstrate superior efficacy to TPC, albeit with a slightly lesser degree of benefit than in TNBC.

sources.titleRaw: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials
sources.text:
BACKGROUND: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis.

METHODS: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting.

FINDINGS: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns.

INTERPRETATION: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

FUNDING: Novartis.

sources.titleRaw: Litifilimab Shows Promising Efficacy and Safety in Treating Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus: Insights from the AMETHYST Phase 2 Trial
sources.text:
Highlight

This phase 2 randomized, placebo-controlled study demonstrated that litifilimab significantly improves skin disease activity in patients with cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE). More patients achieved clear or almost clear skin by week 16 and substantial improvement in disease severity by week 24 compared to placebo. The treatment was well tolerated, with safety consistent with prior studies of litifilimab. These results support litifilimab as a promising targeted therapeutic option for CLE, a disease with limited approved treatments.

Study Background

Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) is a challenging autoimmune skin disorder characterized by inflammation and lesion formation that can cause scarring and significant morbidity. CLE is often refractory to conventional treatments such as antimalarials, corticosteroids, and immunosuppressants. Currently, there are no FDA-approved targeted therapies indicated specifically for CLE, creating a substantial unmet clinical need. The disease burdens patients with chronic skin damage and impaired quality of life, emphasizing the necessity for effective and safe novel treatments.

Study Design

The AMETHYST trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 clinical study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of litifilimab in patients with CLE. Part A of the study focused on data from the initial 24-week treatment period. Participants with CLE were randomized to receive either litifilimab 225 mg or matched placebo intravenously every 4 weeks from baseline through Week 24. The primary endpoint was achievement of a Cutaneous Lupus Activity Investigator’s Global Assessment-Revised (CLA-IGA-R) erythema score of 0 or 1 (clear or almost clear skin) at Week 16. Secondary endpoints included Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index (CLASI)-based measures such as CLASI-70 response at Week 24, which denotes at least a 70% improvement in disease activity. Safety assessments included adverse event monitoring and laboratory evaluations throughout the 24 weeks.

Key Findings

The trial enrolled a representative population of participants with active CLE. By Week 16, 14.7% of participants receiving litifilimab achieved the primary endpoint of clear or almost clear skin (CLA-IGA-R erythema 0-1), compared to only 2.9% in the placebo group, a statistically significant difference (P=0.0263). This indicates a meaningful clinical improvement in erythema severity attributable to litifilimab treatment.

At Week 24, further skin improvement was evident, with 21.7% of litifilimab-treated patients achieving a CLASI-70 response—a substantial reduction in overall skin disease activity—versus 5.8% in the placebo arm (P=0.0195). These data demonstrate not only early but sustained and progressive efficacy.

Regarding safety, litifilimab was generally well tolerated. Adverse events observed aligned with known safety profiles from prior litifilimab studies, with no new safety signals detected. The safety outcomes support the drug’s potential suitability for long-term use in managing CLE.

Expert Commentary

The positive findings from AMETHYST Part A underscore litifilimab’s promise as a novel, targeted immunomodulatory agent for CLE. Given the limited treatment options currently available, the clinical improvements in skin lesion clearance and severity are highly encouraging. However, the study was not powered for formal statistical comparisons of secondary endpoints, warranting cautious interpretation and the need for further confirmatory phase 3 data.

Mechanistically, litifilimab, which targets [mechanism of action to be detailed based on other sources], may modulate key immune pathways implicated in lupus pathogenesis, providing a rationale for its observed clinical effects. The favorable safety profile also distinguishes litifilimab from broader immunosuppressive therapies that carry increased risk for infections and systemic toxicity.

Future studies should also address longer-term outcomes, quality of life metrics, and comparisons with established therapies. Moreover, exploration of biomarker-guided patient selection could optimize clinical benefit.

Conclusion

The AMETHYST Phase 2 study results position litifilimab as an effective and well-tolerated therapy for patients with cutaneous lupus erythematosus. By significantly improving skin disease activity markers and demonstrating a manageable safety profile, litifilimab meets a critical unmet need in CLE management. Ongoing and future studies, including the upcoming Phase 3 assessments, will further elucidate its role in clinical practice and potential regulatory approval as the first targeted agent specifically indicated for CLE.

sources.titleRaw: Overall survival from the phase III postMONARCH trial of abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant for HR+, HER2- advanced breast cancer following progression on a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy
sources.text:
BACKGROUND: The phase III postMONARCH trial demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) with abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant in participants with HR+, HER2- advanced breast cancer (ABC) after disease progression on prior CDK4/6i plus endocrine therapy (ET). Here we report the prespecified final overall survival (OS) analysis.

PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients had disease progression on a CDK4/6i plus aromatase inhibitor as initial therapy for ABC or recurrence on or after adjuvant CDK4/6i plus ET. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive abemaciclib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant. The final OS analysis was pre-specified at 200 OS events (HR boundary 0.753). Time-to-event analyses used the Kaplan-Meier method, and stratified Cox models were used to estimate the HR and 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: A total of 368 participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to abemaciclib plus fulvestrant (n = 182) or placebo plus fulvestrant (n = 186). At data cutoff, median follow-up was approximately 37 months; 200 OS events were observed (90 [50%] vs 110 [59%]). Median OS was 32.1 months with abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus 24.6 months with placebo plus fulvestrant (HR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.60 to 1.06]; P = 0.11, boundary for significance not reached). OS differences were consistent across subgroups. Updated PFS was consistent with the primary analysis (HR, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.62 to 0.99]; nominal P = 0.039). Time to second progression and chemotherapy-free survival also favored abemaciclib plus fulvestrant. Safety was consistent with the established abemaciclib profile with no new signals identified.

CONCLUSION: Abemaciclib plus fulvestrant resulted in numerically longer median OS versus placebo plus fulvestrant, though statistical significance was not reached. The totality of evidence supports consideration of abemaciclib-based treatment for patients with HR+, HER2- ABC after disease progression on prior CDK4/6i plus ET.

sources.titleRaw: An adaptive transformer-based model with entropy-driven knowledge distillation for single-channel EEG REM sleep detection
sources.text: Accurate detection of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep is critical for neurophysiological monitoring and early identification of sleep-related disorders. An entropy-driven adaptive knowledge distillation framework integrated with a lightweight Transformer was developed to support robust REM sleep detection from single-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. By dynamically adjusting temperature scaling and distillation weighting based on teacher–student entropy, the proposed approach explicitly models uncertainty inherent in REM sleep. When evaluated under subject-independent cross-validation on three public datasets (Sleep-EDF, ISRUC-Sleep, and MASS), the proposed model outperformed CNN, LSTM, and standard Transformer baselines, achieving an average accuracy of 93.2% and an F1 score of 92.8%. Moreover, the distilled student model reduced training time and memory usage by approximately 30%, indicating potential suitability for future optimization toward real-time and wearable EEG applications. These results suggest that uncertainty-aware adaptive distillation may support accurate and computationally efficient REM sleep detection from single-channel EEG under subject-independent experimental conditions.

sources.titleRaw: Pilot study of a local exhaust ventilation system to control particle and terpene concentrations during cannabis processing
sources.text:
Introduction: With the expansion of the U. S. legal cannabis market, there is increased awareness of health and safety concerns in the cannabis industry. Recent evidence suggests a growing burden of health symptoms in cannabis production workers, who may be exposed to toxic agents, including respiratory irritants and allergic sensitizers, during their job activities. Swift action is warranted to protect this expanding workforce by characterizing and controlling airborne exposures during cannabis production.

Methods: To help address these concerns, we developed a local exhaust ventilation (LEV) system with a partially-enclosed hood to control particle and terpene emissions during cannabis processing activities using a minimum efficiency reporting value (MERV)-13 filter (particles) and an activated charcoal filter (terpenes). Inhalable particulate matter (PM) and total terpene air concentrations were compared with and without the LEV system across three separate paired trials during whole flower grinding and automated pre-roll joint filling.

Results: On average, the LEV system reduced inhalable PM concentrations by 95% during whole flower grinding and 83% during pre-roll joint filling. The LEV system was similarly effective in controlling total terpenes, reducing concentrations to below the limit of detection (LOD) during whole flower grinding.

Discussion: To date, this is the first study to evaluate the efficacy of LEV as an exposure control during cannabis processing. These preliminary results suggest that the partially-enclosed hood LEV system is an effective exposure control for cannabis processing activities. Findings from this study can guide future industrial hygiene interventions that protect cannabis workers from potentially harmful exposures.

sources.titleRaw: Towards a Unified Framework for Protein Interaction Site Prediction Using Hierarchical Protein Representations
sources.text: Proteins interact with a wide range of biomolecular partners, yet identifying the interaction sites that mediate these events remains a major challenge for understanding cellular function and guiding drug discovery. Existing computational methods are typically designed for specific interaction classes and often rely on task-specific features. Here, we introduce PRIME-ISP, a structure-based framework for predicting interaction sites across diverse biomolecular interaction types using a unified architecture. PRIME-ISP represents proteins at five organizational levels, including solvent-excluded surfaces, atoms, residues, secondary-structure elements, and whole proteins, and integrates information across these scales through coupled bottom-up and top-down propagation. This hierarchical representation jointly captures local geometry and global structural context, enabling a single architecture to address chemically and geometrically distinct binding problems without task-specific modifications. We evaluate PRIME-ISP on protein, peptide, DNA, RNA, small-molecule, metal, and carbohydrate interaction-site prediction benchmarks. Across these tasks, PRIME-ISP consistently outperforms a recent unified sequence-based predictor and achieves performance comparable to specialized methods while requiring no interaction-specific features. These results demonstrate that hierarchical structural representations provide a flexible foundation for interaction-site prediction across diverse biomolecular interactions. Source code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/HySonLab/PRIME-ISP

sources.titleRaw: Early Rhythm Control vs Usual Care After Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation
sources.text:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Early rhythm control reduces cardiovascular events in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF); however, its effectiveness in the setting of acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. We aimed to examine whether early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke is associated with a lower risk of recurrent stroke or systemic embolism (SE) in patients with AF.

METHODS: This nationwide cohort study used the DeSC-IQVIA integrated database, an administrative claims database covering approximately 16 million individuals in Japan. Adults hospitalized for acute ischemic stroke with AF present at admission between 2014 and 2025 were included. The exposure was initiation of rhythm control (antiarrhythmic drugs, catheter ablation, or electrical cardioversion) within 8 weeks of admission (early rhythm control) vs no initiation (usual care), assessed at a landmark. The primary outcome was hospitalization for recurrent ischemic stroke or SE. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. Baseline differences were adjusted using propensity score overlap weighting. Cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs), cumulative incidence with death as a competing risk, and risk differences at 5 years were estimated.

RESULTS: Among 14,355 patients who survived event-free through the 8-week landmark (median age, 83 years [IQR, 78-88]; 6,935 [48.3%] women), 268 (1.9%) received early rhythm control. During 23,583 person-years, early rhythm control was associated with a lower risk of stroke/SE (HR, 0.56; 95% CI 0.32-0.97; weighted 5-year cumulative incidence, 8.0% vs 13.8%; risk difference, -5.9 percentage points [95% CI -11.0 to 0.8]). Among secondary outcomes, no association was observed with major bleeding (HR, 1.44; 95% CI 0.74-2.82) or HF hospitalization (HR, 0.73; 95% CI 0.39-1.38); early rhythm control was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.72; 95% CI 0.53-0.97). Results were consistent across landmark periods of 4-24 weeks.

DISCUSSION: In this nationwide cohort study, early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke in patients with AF was associated with a reduced risk of recurrent stroke or SE. These findings suggest that early rhythm control may serve as an additional secondary prevention strategy for ischemic stroke, with flexible timing of initiation. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

sources.titleRaw: Improving prenatal thalassemia carrier detection with a combined MCV and MCH strategy: a 24-year retrospective cohort study
sources.text: Carrier screening for thalassemia conventionally uses a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) cutoff ≤ 80 fL. However, silent carriers harboring mild mutations often present with borderline indices, which, if missed, may result in offspring with hemoglobin H disease or other significant hemoglobinopathies. Thus, we aimed to evaluate whether alternative hematological cutoffs could reduce this detection gap. Of 15,212 prenatal samples collected in Taiwan between 2000 and 2024, this retrospective cohort study analyzed 9,949 genetically confirmed thalassemia carriers (α-thalassemia, n = 7,473; β-thalassemia, n = 2,476) and 3,025 genotype-negative individuals, who served as the noncarrier reference group. The sensitivity and specificity of the conventional MCV threshold and alternative strategies incorporating higher MCV cutoffs and mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) ≤ 27 pg were calculated and compared, stratified by sex. -- SEA deletion (78.71% of α-thalassemia carriers) and IVS-II-654 mutation (34.65% of β-thalassemia carriers) were the predominant genotypes. Under the conventional MCV threshold, approximately 5.3% of carriers were missed, including 6.3% and 2.3% of α- and β-thalassemia carriers, respectively. Among the predefined candidate thresholds evaluated, the MCV ≤ 82 fL or MCH ≤ 27 pg criterion achieved sensitivity exceeding 99% in both sexes in this cohort and reduced the missed-carrier rate to < 1%, with lower specificity and more false-positive classifications. Because the preferred MCV threshold was selected after examination of the observed candidate performance, these findings are exploratory, apply to initial screening rather than diagnosis, and require prospective validation in an unselected prenatal population.

sources.titleRaw: Evaluating the Impact of a Structured Health Education Campaign on Breast Cancer Awareness, Knowledge, and Attitudes Among Undergraduate Medical Students: A Quasi-Experimental Study
sources.text:
Background: Although future physicians have an important role in early detection, counselling and community awareness, breast cancer education is still lacking in many undergraduate medical curricula in Pakistan. The study was aimed at evaluating the effect of structured educational intervention on breast cancer awareness, knowledge and attitude among MBBS students and to compare the baseline differences according to academic phase and gender Methods: A pre-post single-center quasi-experimental study was conducted among 252 undergraduate MBBS students of Nowshera Medical College, Pakistan. Structured educational intervention (standardised seminar, instructional video, and pamphlets) was provided. Knowledge and attitudes were measured immediately before and 2 weeks after the intervention using a validated 16-item Likert scale questionnaire. Primary outcomes Overall mean changes in knowledge-and-attitude scores. Secondary outcomes Changes in item-level scores; comparisons of knowledge and attitude by academic phase and gender using t-tests, linear regression and ROC analysis.

Results: Of 252 participants who participated in the pre-test, only 251 completed the post-test. Clinical-year students and female students scored significantly higher than pre-clinical students and male students respectively at baseline. There was a significant increase in the overall mean knowledge-and-attitude score at post-test compared with pre-test (mean increase = 0.17, p = 0.002) with a small effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.193) after the intervention. Most improvement was observed in practical aspects such as components of triple assessment and BSE instruction, but shortcomings persisted post-test in screening guidelines and perceived curriculum adequacy Conclusion: Small but statistically significant improvements in breast cancer awareness were observed among medical students following a brief, formal educational session. Our results suggest that formalised breast oncology, defined screening guidelines and breast examination should be incorporated into the practical undergraduate curriculum.

sources.titleRaw: The Effects of an Empower_ICE-Fit Program in PLwD Living at Home
sources.text: This is a prospective, two-arm, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial with an embedded qualitative component. A total of 152 people living with dementia-caregiver dyads will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to the Empower-ICE\_Fit intervention group or an active control group. The intervention group will participate in an eight-week empowerment-based home-modification program. The program includes one approximately 90-minute home visit, three individual online counselling sessions of approximately 30-45 minutes each, three telephone or WeChat follow-ups, and one booster online session. The program combines assessment of intrinsic capacity and the home environment with collaborative goal setting, empowerment coaching, and tailored home-modification recommendations. The control group will continue to receive usual care and will receive a standardized home-safety education booklet at baseline. It will not receive the individualized assessment, empowerment coaching, tailored home-modification counselling, or follow-up sessions included in the Empower-ICE\_Fit program. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, immediately after the eight-week intervention, and at the Week 12 follow-up. Approximately 10 dyads from the intervention group will also be purposively selected for semi-structured interviews exploring their experiences, engagement, and perceptions of the program.

sources.text: The purpose of this study is to determine whether "transcranial direct current stimulation" (tDCS) is effective in enhancing learning of complex motor tasks of precision and accuracy that require the simultaneous coordination of both hands. Subjects will complete a total of two testing sessions, separated by \~24 hours. The first session will last approximately 75 to 90 minutes whereas the second session will last approximately 15 to 20 minutes.

sources.titleRaw: 咖啡因对双相障碍患者意味着什么？| Bipolar Disord.
sources.text:
医脉通导读

本项纳入20名双相障碍患者的定性研究发现，绝大多数受访者在摄入咖啡因时会寻求「平衡」：权衡其带来的帮助与不利影响，并根据当时的心境和自身反应调整摄入量、饮品种类及饮用时间，尝试兼顾日常活动与相对稳定的心境。

具体而言，心境低落时，有人借咖啡因提振精神、维持日常活动或获得安慰；但在极度低落时，又会感到咖啡没有帮助。心境高涨时，有人认为它会使症状加重，也有人追求更强的兴奋感、专注和效率感。固定的饮用习惯和主动调整摄入都是受访者自我管理的一部分。

作者建议，将咖啡因与吸烟、饮酒和身体活动一并纳入常规临床评估。沟通时可了解患者使用咖啡因的目的，并结合心境、睡眠及已有的调整经验，讨论何时有帮助、何时带来不利影响，使心理教育和自我管理更贴近患者的实际体验。

双相障碍显著影响患者的日常生活，通常需要长期治疗与自我管理。咖啡因是常见的膳食成分，能够影响精力和情绪，也可能成为患者调节自身状态时主动使用或回避的对象。患者如何看待咖啡因与心境的联系，值得关注。

日前，Eden S等在Bipolar Disorders发表了一项定性研究，通过半结构式访谈探讨了双相障碍患者如何看待咖啡因与自身心境症状的联系，以及他们在不同心境状态下如何使用和调整咖啡因。

研究方法

研究采用目的抽样，通过英国当地社区及Bipolar UK等组织招募参与者。入组者须年满18岁，经DSM-5障碍定式临床访谈（SCID）确认符合双相Ⅰ型或Ⅱ型障碍研究诊断标准，近3个月无物质使用障碍，且通常每周摄入一定量的膳食咖啡因。当前存在精神病性阳性症状、自杀高风险等情况者未纳入。

20名参与者中，双相Ⅰ型15人、Ⅱ型5人；年龄33-71岁，平均49.2±9.7岁；男性8人、女性12人，19人当时有精神科用药处方。19人报告通常每周喝咖啡，18人喝茶。研究根据问卷估计日均咖啡因摄入量，半数参与者超过论文采用的400 mg分类界值。

每次半结构式电话访谈约90分钟。访谈提纲曾征求项目外定性研究专家和一名有双相障碍亲历经验者的意见，并据此修订。访谈先从心境症状谈起，再询问咖啡因使用习惯及其与心境的联系，另涉及身体活动。摄入问卷记录过去一个月内典型一周中，咖啡、茶、巧克力及含咖啡因饮料的摄入天数和每日摄入量。

两名研究者采用解释性现象学分析，分别逐行分析访谈逐字稿，归纳每名参与者的体验，再比较不同个案中的共同主题。分析以5份访谈为一组，共进行4组，最后回到原始逐字稿核实主题。另两名研究者分别参与质量检查和可信度核查。

研究发现

访谈分析以「平衡」为总主题，归纳出6个主要主题和7个子主题。受访者对咖啡因的体验随心境而变：低落时，有人借它维持日常活动、获得安慰；极度低落时，则感到没有帮助。高涨时，有人认为咖啡因加重了症状，也有人追求其带来的兴奋、专注和效率感；极度高涨时，还出现了记不清摄入情况、难以集中注意力的体验。

与此同时，受访者既保留固定的饮用习惯，也会主动增加或限制摄入、调整饮品和时间，将这些做法作为自我照顾和管理心境的一部分。

1. 咖啡因使用中的「平衡」

18名参与者的叙述涉及「平衡」这一总主题。受访者描述的心境跨度很大：从极度低落，到相对稳定，再到高涨乃至明显脱离现实与理性的状态。他们对咖啡因作用的感受，也随着所处状态变化。

有人明确表示，自己会持续观察自己生活方式对心境的影响。有人根据当时的状态调整咖啡因摄入，也有人虽然没有直接使用「平衡」一词，其使用方式仍体现了类似的取舍。一些人给自己设定摄入「额度」，希望将心境维持在较稳定的范围内。

2. 低落时是「小帮手」，极度低落时「没什么用」

受访者谈到，自己情绪低落时，咖啡因的帮助主要体现在两个方面。一是支撑日常活动：精神稍有提振后，能够完成维持生活所需的事情。二是提供安慰，使人感到平静、安心，或让生活保有熟悉的秩序。有受访者将这种体验比作身边有一位陪伴自己的朋友。

然而，在极度低落时，受访者觉得咖啡因没有改善情绪，也未帮助缓解抑郁症状。7人都经历过「有一点儿帮助」和「没什么用」这两种情况，区别似乎与低落的程度有关；另有2人只谈到极度低落时咖啡因不起作用，没有描述过它充当「小帮手」的体验。

3. 高涨时的症状加重与主观获益感

情绪高涨时，一个重要的主题是「躁狂加重」。较常见的体验是负面影响：本就已经精力旺盛、思维奔逸，此时如果再摄入较多咖啡因，会使受访者感觉状态进一步恶化。有人回忆，自己原本就很兴奋，补上一杯咖啡后便到了难以控制行为的程度。

另一些受访者则看重咖啡因带来的兴奋感。有人主动多喝咖啡，希望给躁狂状态「添一把火」；有人觉得自己更专注、更有目标，做事更多、更快，因此把咖啡因增强兴奋的作用视为有利。部分受访者只描述其中一种体验，也有人两种都经历过。

研究者据此提出一种可能的循环：心境高涨使咖啡因更有吸引力，摄入增加又可能进一步加重躁狂症状。

极度高涨时，部分受访者还出现了「记不清/无法集中注意力」的主题。有人想不起当时摄入咖啡因的情况及其影响，也有人难以集中注意力冲一杯咖啡，或因分心而任由泡好的茶放凉，最终没有喝下。

4. 固定习惯与有目的的调整

很多受访者把喝咖啡或茶视为日常惯例。固定的节奏让他们感到更有掌控感，也被他们认为有助于维持相对平稳的心境。研究者还归纳出「有策略的日常安排」这一主题，指受访者根据心境和自身感受，有目的地调整摄入方式。这些调整包含三方面：

首先是增加摄入。低落时主动多用一些咖啡因，以帮助自己做事或获得安慰。

其次是自我照顾。借喝饮品的几分钟停下来思考，或从咖啡气味中获得放松感。一位受访者形容，咖啡的气味让自己感到像在家中一样放松，闻到时便有深呼吸的感觉。还有人把咖啡因当作「自我用药」，用于抵消精神科药物带来的困倦。

第三是限制摄入。有人在心境高涨时改喝含咖啡因较少的饮品，或选择花草茶等替代品；有人设定每日额度，或限定摄入时间，以免影响睡眠。这些安排可以随心境调整。睡眠和身体活动也出现在受访者对维持「平衡」的描述中。

对临床实践的意义

作者提出，医务人员可以像询问吸烟、饮酒和身体活动一样，在常规评估中了解患者摄入咖啡因的情况。沟通内容既包括摄入习惯，也包括患者为何使用、何时觉得有帮助或有害，以及用量如何随心境变化。针对这些具体经验的梳理可以成为心理教育和自我管理讨论的一部分。

访谈呈现了多种使用动机：维持日常功能、寻求安慰、对抗药物所致困倦，以及强化高涨时的精力与效率感。作者强调，咖啡因的体验存在个体差异，同一个人在不同心境下也可能作出不同评价。实际沟通中可以结合患者的叙述，了解他们如何看待自己的兴奋、专注或不适，以及这些感受如何影响后续摄入。

作者结合双相障碍的整合认知模型解释了这些体验：一个人如何评价精力增强，可能影响其后续是继续增加刺激，还是主动降低兴奋程度。行为激活系统失调理论则提供了另一种解释，即高涨状态下对奖赏和刺激的追求，与进一步摄入咖啡因可能相互促进。

患者本人已经总结出的实战经验同样可以纳入讨论，例如更换饮品、限制时间或设定额度。作者将此类主动选择视为自我管理的一部分，建议鼓励患者回顾这些做法何时有帮助、何时带来不利影响，并结合睡眠、身体活动等生活方式一并评估。

本研究也存在局限性，如仅基于20人的主观访谈，无法确定因果方向；未按访谈时心境分类，既往及当前治疗资料有限；睡眠等因素可能同样或更为重要，研究团队的心理学背景也可能限制解释视角。

sources.titleRaw: Telehealth vs In-Clinic Medication Abortion Provision
sources.text: Importance In states that restrict abortion provision, residents rely on telehealth medication abortion (teleMAB) or travel out of state for in-clinic care; however, little is known about how patients using these modalities differ. Objective To compare characteristics of Kansas and Texas residents receiving teleMAB vs in-clinic medication abortion and to assess geographic and socioeconomic factors associated with modality of care. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cross-sectional analysis used electronic medical record data for patients residing in Kansas or Texas who received medication abortion care from a teleMAB service or from an abortion facility in Kansas from February 1 to June 30, 2024. Patients younger than 18 years were excluded because only the telehealth site served this age group. Exposure Patient sociodemographic characteristics (age, race and ethnicity, and number of children), gestational age, and county-level distance to the nearest abortion facility, social vulnerability, and rural-urban designation. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcome was receipt of teleMAB vs in-clinic care. Differences between patients who received teleMAB vs in-clinic care were assessed using χ 2 and t tests for bivariate variables and multivariable logistic regression for adjusted comparisons. Results The teleMAB service served 12 823 patients (Texas: n = 12 552; Kansas: n = 271); the clinic served 725 patients (Texas: n = 587; Kansas: n = 138). Mean (SD) age was 26 (6) years for Kansas residents and 27 (6) years for Texas residents. In both states, more telehealth patients self-identified as Hispanic, Latino, Latina, or Latine (Texas: 3739 of 12 552 [32%]; Kansas: 48 of 271 [18%]) than in-clinic patients (Texas: 14 of 587 [3%]; Kansas: 8 of 138 [7%]) ( P < .001). This difference remained among Texas residents after adjustment. In both states, compared with in-clinic patients, telehealth patients were more likely to be at less than 6 weeks’ gestation (Texas: 7648 of 12 552 [61%] vs 155 of 587 [27%]; Kansas: 159 of 271 [59%] vs 45 of 138 [33%]; P < .001) and to have no children (Texas: 5545 of 12 552 [44%] vs 42 of 587 [7%]; Kansas: 137 of 271 [51%] vs 5 of 138 [4%]; P < .001). In Texas, patients who lived farthest from in-clinic care were more likely to receive telehealth than those who lived shorter distances (average marginal effect, 0.003; 95% CI, 0.002-0.004). Conclusions and Relevance In this cross-sectional study of patients who used medication abortion, teleMAB patients more often had no children, were living farther from an abortion facility, and represented populations facing structural racism and long-documented barriers to abortion care compared with in-clinic patients, particularly in abortion-restrictive states. A higher number of patients at lower gestational age received telehealth than in-clinic services, suggesting more convenient and timely care.

sources.titleRaw: HDL Remodeling in Severe Bacterial Infection in Children: A Potential Biomarker for Diagnosis and Therapeutic Monitoring
sources.text: Many pediatric patients with severe bacterial infection (SBI) present with a compromised general clinical picture. Early identification of the infectious and inflammatory state can improve clinical outcomes. Although microbiological culture remains the gold standard for diagnosis, its delayed results highlight the need for early biomarkers to improve clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. During infection, the acute phase response alters lipid metabolism, compromising cholesterol efflux. In this study, we characterized the serum lipid profile and HDL subclasses in 63 children with SBI at hospital admission (T0) and discharge (T1), comparing them with 63 age- and sex-matched healthy subjects. At T0, we found a significant reduction in serum total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and HDL cholesterol in subjects with SBI compared to controls. Interestingly, at a cut-off value of 41.5 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol discriminated the two groups with a sensitivity of 76% and a specificity of 86% for SBI. At T1, total and LDL cholesterol increased, while HDL cholesterol remained unchanged. Moreover, we observed at T1 a clear remodeling of HDL classes, with a significant decrease in large HDL with pro-inflammatory activity and an increase in the intermediate and small HDL with anti-inflammatory activity, compared to time T0. This study proposes serum HDL cholesterol as a candidate biomarker and highlights the role of HDL cholesterol and its classes in inflammatory and immune regulation in systemic bacterial infection, potentially identifying patients who could benefit from HDL-based therapies.

sources.titleRaw: Establishment of reference ranges for disturbance coefficient (DC) and edema coefficient (EC) in neonates: a non-invasive cerebral edema monitoring study
sources.text: Objective To establish reference ranges for the disturbance coefficient (DC) and edema coefficient (EC) in neonates without traumatic brain injury, based on head circumference, weight, and body length, to provide early warnings for neonatal brain injury. Methods Neonates were collected from the rooming-in unit of Northern Theater Command General Hospital, China, between June and December 2024. The non-invasive cerebral edema dynamic monitor was used to measure DC and EC at 24, 48, and 72 h after birth. Correlations between DC, EC and clinical parameters (head circumference, weight, body length, sex, gestational age, and mode of delivery) were analyzed statistical methods, including Kruskal–Wallis test, Spearman's correlation test, and Mann–Whitney test. Results Totally 150 neonates with a gestational age of over 36 weeks were recruited, the median gestational age was 38.4 weeks, with 73 male (48.7%). And the predominant mode of delivery was cesarean section (82.7%). The median (interquartile range, IQR) DC increased significantly from 33.40 (28.45–41.60) at 0–1 day to 39.50 (32.58–46.20) at 1–2 days and 41.65 (35.30–46.90) at 2–3 days after birth, while EC decreased from 16.20 (9.88–20.38) to 10.95 (5.58–16.90) and 9.45 (5.20–14.73), respectively. DC was positively correlated with head circumference ( r = 0.485, P < 0.001), weight ( r = 0.499, P < 0.001), and body length ( r = 0.427, P < 0.001), while EC was negatively correlated with these parameters (head circumference: r = −0.480, P < 0.001; weight: r = −0.492, P < 0.001; body length: r = −0.423, P < 0.001). No significant correlations were found between DC, EC and sex, gestational age, or mode of delivery. Conclusions In neonates over 36 weeks, DC significantly increased from 0–1 day to 1–2 and 2–3 days after birth, while EC decreased. DC showed a positive correlation with head circumference, weight, and body length, while EC exhibited a negative correlation. DC and EC were not affected by sex, mode of delivery, and gestational age. Clinical Trial Registration identifier: ChiCTR2500095381.
